clauses: "Yes, indeed, you may go," said Aunt Annie; "but what will you put the roots and earth in while you are making the garden?"

note: postposed speaker in c0 (said Aunt Annie) and c1 (said Bessie) = order!=role meaning-required; c2 preposed (Her aunt laughed and said) is surface-decidable; Her aunt=Aunt_Annie coref

clauses: The squirrels peeped out of their holes at Bessie.

note: Bessie role variation patient(peeped at)->agent(jumped)->experiencer(laughed); all surface-decidable, position matches role in each clause; used for canonical-construction balance

clauses: She was back at the house in a few minutes, calling, "Mother! mother! auntie! Who wants me?"

Then Bessie's mother kissed her, and told her to obey her kind aunt while she was gone.
note: c1 postposed speaker (said her mother) = meaning-required; She=Bessie, her mother/Bessie's mother coref; Bessie shifts agent->patient across clauses

clauses: "No; don't laugh, Aunt Annie; to leave your nice basket out of doors all night; and now it will be soaked and ruined in this--this--beautiful rain."

clauses: George Ellet had a bright silver dollar for a New-year gift.

clauses: He rang the doorbell.

clauses: Father and Charles went out a little way from the shore in a boat, and fished, while Lucy and I gathered sea mosses.

clauses: Robert and Henry were going home from school, when, on turning a corner, Robert cried out, "A fight! let us go and see!"
"No," said Henry; "let us go quietly home and not meddle with this quarrel."
"You are a coward, and afraid to go," said Robert, and off he ran.
note: c1 preposed (said Henry, surface-decidable); c2 postposed (said Robert, meaning-required); sets up the courage/cowardice role reversal completed in robert_henry_rescue_2

clauses: A few days after, Robert was bathing with some schoolmates, and got out of his depth.

note: role reversal payoff: Robert agent(bathing)->patient(sinking, needing rescue); Henry patient(called coward, c1 object of 'called')->agent(rescuer); him(c1)=Robert coref; surface-decidable throughout but high-value role-VARIATION discriminator

clauses: "What a baby!" said Joe, his elder brother, who was reading on the sofa.

clauses: Herbert took up one of the blocks and threw it fiercely at pussy.

"No, no, no!" said she, "you sha'n't hurt pussy! She did n't mean to do it!"
note: c2 postposed (said she) meaning-required, she=Hetty by turn structure; pussy=the cat coref (animate non-human patient); Herbert as thrower(agent) vs Hetty as rescuer(agent) contrastive roles toward same patient

clauses: "This is a great deal better than crying, is n't it?" said papa.

clauses: "I should like to go with you very much," replied Susan, with a sigh; "but I can not finish the task grandmother set me to do."

clauses: "How tiresome it must be to stay at home to work on a holiday!" said one of the girls, with a toss of her head.

clauses: Henry Bond was about ten years old when his father died.

clauses: "I couldn't see mother, nor the baby, nor the flowers, nor the horses, nor anything," added Harry, growing warmer and warmer.

clauses: Hugh Idle loved to do only what was agreeable, and took no delight in labor of any kind.

"This will never do for me," thought Hugh; "I'll run off, and try to find my way home."

clauses: "O Andy!" said little Jenny Murdock, "I'm so glad you came along this way. I can't get over."

note: all three postposed quotatives meaning-required; two named entities alternating; feeds into jenny_andrew_bridge_byagent for the animate/inanimate byagent contrast

clauses: She had crossed the creek in search of wild flowers, and when she wished to return had found the bridge removed, as Andrew supposed, by old Donald McKensie, who pastured his cows on this side of the creek.

clauses: So infuriated were the soldiers that, when the men returned to take up the dead, they prepared to fire again, but were checked by Preston, while the Twenty-ninth Regiment appeared under arms in King Street.
